issues.description: The template Meal constructor has its parameters in the order (String[] ingredients, String name), but the problem statement UML and the provided solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients). This mismatch will cause compile errors for students using the example code in Main and will confuse them about the correct constructor signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the template Meal class to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) so it matches the problem statement and the solution. Alternatively, adjust the example usages in Main to match the template constructor, but aligning the template with the spec (name first, ingredients second) is recommended.

issues.description: Constructor parameter order for Meal is inconsistent: the problem statement (UML) and the solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) but the template implements Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch breaks the mapping between the problem description, the provided Main usage, and the template implementation, causing unnecessary confusion about how to construct a Meal.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor signature to match the problem and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and adjust parameter names and any call sites (e.g., Main) accordingly so all artifacts use the same constructor order and meaning.
